newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-PLAY RESUMES IN U.S. OPEN AFTER WEATHER DELAY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PLAY RESUMES IN U.S. OPEN AFTER WEATHER DELAY.

text.p: Play resumed in the third round of the U.S. Open on Saturday evening after a two-hour delay caused by a brief but severe thunderstorm.
The players returned to the soaked Congressional Country Club course at 7:09 p.m. EDT (2309 GMT) with Tom Lehman and Jeff Maggert tied for the lead at five under par.
Maggert, who had just made the turn, and Lehman, playing the ninth, were two strokes ahead of veteran Hal Sutton, who was playing with Maggert, and young Stewart Cink, who was in Lehman's group.

Lehman, however, was in trouble on the ninth, where he drove into the deep rough and could not advance his ball very far on his second shot -- leaving him a very long approach to the green on the 607-yard hole.
It was the second time in two days that the championship was halted due to weather.
The second round was suspended for two hours, 18 minutes Friday due to the threat of lightning and the round had to be completed Saturday morning before the third round could begin.
It was not known whether the third round would be completed on Saturday due to the delay.
